question.text: In the standard private-equity deal pipeline described in Ch 11, at which stage does the PE firm first require the investee company to sign a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA)?

answer.text: After signing the term sheet, before virtual data-room access
After the Shareholders' Agreement is executed
Only at the Final Investment Memorandum stage
After gaining initial interest in the start-up, before examining confidential records

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the PE deal pipeline, after gaining initial interest in the start-up the PE firm signs an NDA so the team can assess and examine the start-up's confidential records before proceeding to detailed due diligence. Skipping the NDA risks the firm receiving price-sensitive information without confidentiality protection. The Trap: Option A puts the NDA after the term sheet — but the term sheet itself follows preliminary info access already covered by the NDA. Option B (post-SHA) is at the end of the deal cycle, far too late. Option C (FIM stage) is also far too late since the FIM is prepared after due diligence on confidential records. Note: NDA is at the start of the engagement, immediately after initial interest and before any access to confidential records of the investee company.
